hunks.baseline: I’d only raised my spear. So where was this sharp whistle now piercing my ears coming from?
hunks.sol: I’d only raised my spear. So where had that whistle cutting through the air beside my ear come from?

hunks.baseline: In that brief instant, split into even smaller fragments, I turned and brought my spearhead down.
hunks.sol: In that fraction of an instant, I turned and brought my spearhead down.

hunks.baseline: The pressure bursting along the spearhead knocked away a dozen or so daggers. At the same moment, two swords came slashing in from either side, aiming for my upper and lower body at once.
hunks.sol: The force bursting from the spearhead knocked away a dozen or so daggers. At the same moment, two swords came in from either side, driving toward my upper and lower body.

hunks.baseline: An alert sounded to tell me the durability of my Fire Dragon Armor had dropped, and a considerable stream of blood gushed from my thigh.
hunks.sol: An alert warned me that the Fire Dragon Armor’s durability had dropped, and blood spurted from my thigh.

hunks.baseline: But if this was the price of fending off a surprise attack from three S-rank Hunters, it was a pretty good deal.
hunks.sol: Still, that was a decent price for fending off a surprise attack by three S-rank Hunters.

hunks.baseline: Blood sprayed belatedly, soaking the ground. A middle-aged man and woman stared wide-eyed as they saw their comrade collapse, his chest split wide open.
hunks.sol: Blood sprayed belatedly across the ground. A middle-aged man and woman stared as their comrade collapsed, his chest split wide open.

hunks.baseline: It had all happened so quickly that I hadn’t had time to see who they were. But now that I was facing them, I recognized them all too well.
hunks.sol: It had happened too fast for me to see who’d attacked. Now that I faced them, though, I knew those faces all too well.

hunks.baseline: S-rank Hunters who each represented their country and stood as symbols of humanity.
hunks.sol: S-rank Hunters who represented their respective countries and stood as symbols of humanity.

hunks.baseline: At my greeting, tinged with a hollow laugh, the middle-aged pair swallowed hard.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged pair swallowed hard at my greeting.

hunks.baseline: Fernando Lucas, Brazil’s S-rank Hunter, had made the reckless choice to aim for my chest. Even as he spilled an enormous amount of blood, he was fumbling for a potion with trembling hands.
hunks.sol: Fernando Lucas, Brazil’s S-rank Hunter, had made the reckless choice to aim for my chest. Even as blood poured from his wound, he pulled out a potion with a trembling hand.

hunks.baseline: He looked so desperate that I spoke to him in a warm voice, like the male lead in a romance movie.
hunks.sol: He looked so desperate that I spoke to him in the warm voice of a romantic lead.

hunks.baseline: “But if you hang in there until this is all over, I’ll treat you. I’ll even make sure you get a nice prison. All right, then. Deal.”
hunks.sol: “But hold on until this is over and I’ll get you treated. I’ll even find you a nice prison. All right? Promise.”

hunks.baseline: Fernando Lucas stared at me blankly, as if he’d forgotten the pain.
hunks.sol: Fernando Lucas stared at me as though he’d forgotten the pain.

hunks.baseline: Then, with lightning speed, he shoved the potion in his hand into his mouth.
hunks.sol: Then he shoved the potion into his mouth with lightning speed.

hunks.baseline: Still in its bottle. Without even taking off the cap.
hunks.sol: Bottle and all, without even removing the cap.

hunks.baseline: *Crack! Thud!*
hunks.sol: *Crunch! Thud!*

hunks.baseline: Shattered glass and potion spilled into his open mouth.
hunks.sol: Shattered glass and potion poured into his open mouth.

hunks.baseline: But even the highest-grade potion, capable of restoring torn organs in the blink of an eye, couldn’t bring back someone who was already dead.
hunks.sol: But even the finest potion could only heal torn organs in the blink of an eye. It couldn’t bring back the dead.
I murmured to Fernando Lucas’s corpse, a hole through his forehead where my Finger Qi had struck.

hunks.baseline: I murmured softly, looking at Fernando Lucas’s corpse, his forehead pierced by my Finger Qi. Just then, the two middle-aged Hunters beside him—slightly luckier than the man who’d gone to the next world first, and much more skilled—spoke with stiff faces.
hunks.sol: The two middle-aged Hunters who’d survived him—slightly luckier and far more skilled—spoke with rigid faces.

hunks.baseline: “It’s not too late, Jin. If you stop, we’ll withdraw. There’s no need for more sacrifices here, is there?”
hunks.sol: “It’s not too late, Jin. If you stop, we’ll withdraw. There’s no need for any more sacrifices, is there?”

hunks.baseline: For a moment, I was at a loss for words. Then I looked around.
At the National Assembly, its interior still being stained red. At Michael Silbert, lying on the floor and twitching like an insect. Finally, at the two people standing before him.
hunks.sol: For a moment, I had no words. I looked around the National Assembly, where the floor was still being stained with blood, then at Michael Silbert, sprawled there and twitching like an insect.

hunks.baseline: Then I thrust out my spear.
hunks.sol: Finally, I looked at the two people standing in front of him and thrust out my spear.

hunks.baseline: One of the few lessons I’d learned by now was that you didn’t have to answer every stupid thing people said.
hunks.sol: One of the few lessons I’d learned was that I didn’t have to answer every stupid thing people said.

hunks.baseline: Even if they didn’t know martial arts, they were S-rank Hunters who’d seen more than enough combat.
hunks.sol: They might not know martial arts, but they were S-rank Hunters with plenty of combat behind them.

hunks.baseline: With a sharp, startled gasp, the two barely evaded my attack and landed in front of and behind me.
But after the spearhead had come flying without warning, their eyes sank heavily.
hunks.sol: They gasped and barely dodged the attack, landing in front of and behind me. The spearhead had come without warning, and their eyes had turned grave.

hunks.baseline: “So this is your answer?”
hunks.sol: “So that’s your answer?”

hunks.baseline: “Wait. Don’t provoke him for no reason. Right now, we need to save Michael first—”
hunks.sol: “Wait. Don’t provoke him. We need to save Michael first—”

hunks.baseline: The woman understood the situation far better than the man did. But she was just as laughable.
hunks.sol: The woman had a much better grasp of the situation than the man, but she made me want to laugh just as much.

hunks.baseline: *What the hell had they been doing all this time? How much had they done to bring things to this point?*
hunks.sol: *What the hell had they been doing all this time? How much had they done for things to come to this?*

hunks.baseline: There’d been a time when I didn’t know anything, either.
hunks.sol: There’d been a time when I hadn’t known anything, either.

hunks.baseline: A time when I’d gone mechanically back and forth between Gates and my goshiwon. A time when I fought monsters for money rather than out of a sense of duty as a Hunter, yet still felt vaguely offended whenever I heard someone say Hunters had fallen into corruption.
hunks.sol: Back when I’d gone mechanically from Gates to my goshiwon and back. I’d fought monsters for money, not out of some sense of duty as a Hunter, yet I’d still felt vaguely offended whenever I heard someone say Hunters had become corrupt.

hunks.baseline: And there was no going back.
hunks.sol: There was no going back.

hunks.baseline: It didn’t matter how great their achievements were, or how much strength they could contribute to the coming war.
hunks.sol: I didn’t care what they’d accomplished or how valuable they might be in the war to come.

hunks.baseline: If we didn’t cut out these tumors rooted deep in society, humanity would collapse before it even got the chance to fight the monsters.
hunks.sol: If we didn’t cut out the tumors rooted deep in society, humanity would collapse before it could fight the monsters.

hunks.baseline: Right before my eyes stood another Lee Jungryong, another Go Jun, another Michael Silbert.
hunks.sol: Another Lee Jungryong. Another Go Jun. Another Michael Silbert. They were right in front of me.

hunks.baseline: The moment they turned their weapons against us despite the ugly truth having been exposed, they became tumors that had to be cut out.
hunks.sol: The moment they’d turned their weapons against us despite the ugly truth being exposed, they’d become tumors that had to be cut out.

hunks.baseline: I charged without hesitation toward the people who’d once been the objects of my admiration and respect.
hunks.sol: I charged without hesitation at the people I’d once admired and respected.

hunks.baseline: It was ironic. Pain itself was what tormented people, and yet they couldn’t feel it when death was near.
hunks.sol: It was ironic. Pain tormented people, yet as death drew near, they could no longer feel it.

hunks.baseline: And…… that numbness was more frightening than any terrible pain.
hunks.sol: And…… that numbness was more frightening than any pain.

hunks.baseline: His lips were slightly parted, but he couldn’t even groan. The strength was draining from his arms and legs, from which powerful energy had surged without pause. The blood that had soaked his body and was now sloshing around him felt dull and distant.
hunks.sol: His lips parted, but he couldn’t even groan. The strength was draining from the arms and legs that had once brimmed with power. Even the blood soaking his body and sloshing around him felt distant.

hunks.baseline: If he was going to fall like this, what had his life been for?
hunks.sol: If this was how he fell, what had he lived for?

hunks.baseline: Instead of a hollow laugh, a bloody bubble welled in his mouth. His head tipped to the side as if he were collapsing, and he saw the corpse of a man frozen with his eyes wide open.
hunks.sol: Blood frothed in his mouth where a bitter laugh should have been. His head lolled to one side, and he saw a corpse lying there with its eyes wide open.

hunks.baseline: He’d been a delinquent who belonged to a Brazilian gang from childhood, and he had the enthusiastic support of South America’s lower classes. Over the past ten years, Michael Silbert had done him various “favors.”
hunks.sol: Fernando had been a gang member since childhood, a delinquent who’d won fervent support among South America’s poor. Over the past ten years, Michael Silbert had done him various “favors.”

hunks.baseline: *It started out small.*
hunks.sol: *It started small.*

hunks.baseline: But everything dulled with time, and each repetition made it grow like a snowball.
hunks.sol: But time dulled everything, and each repetition made it snowball.

hunks.baseline: He’d eliminated a powerful rival and made it look like an accidental death. He’d used a politician with connections to him to bury tax-evasion charges. He’d even kidnapped a brave journalist and his family when the man was preparing an article about how the hero of Brazil’s poor secretly ran a gang and made a fortune on the side.

hunks.baseline: The others now spilling blood and dying for him in every corner were no different.
hunks.sol: The others spilling blood and dying for him throughout the chamber were no different.

hunks.baseline: *No. They weren’t doing this for me.*
hunks.sol: *No. They aren’t doing this for me.*

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert knew.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert knew why they fought.

hunks.baseline: They were fighting for themselves.
They knew there was too much to lose if they admitted and accepted everything now.
hunks.sol: They fought for themselves. They had too much to lose by admitting everything now.

hunks.baseline: In the end, he and the others had been no more than filth wallowing together in the same pit.
hunks.sol: In the end, he and they were nothing but filth seething in the same pit.

hunks.baseline: But thanks to that—thanks to how long he’d indulged their greed and ambition—Michael Silbert had bought himself a little time.
hunks.sol: But because he’d spent so long satisfying their greed and ambition, they’d bought him a little time.

hunks.sol: Precious time to cast off the human bonds he’d clung to until the end and become the Demon King.

hunks.baseline: The blood that had filled the crater rippled like a wave. Through his blurred vision, he saw a spearhead flash through the air and graze the neck of a middle-aged man.
hunks.sol: The blood pooled in the crater rippled like a wave. Through his blurred vision, Michael saw a spearhead flash across the air and pass over a middle-aged man’s neck.

hunks.baseline: A body fell with a wet thud, and a head rolled over to meet his gaze.
hunks.sol: A body fell with a wet thud. A head rolled toward him, its eyes meeting his.

hunks.baseline: The smell of blood wafting from the charred-black cross-section seemed as sweet as chocolate. That wasn’t merely his imagination.
hunks.sol: The scent of blood rising from the blackened cut, as though it had been seared, smelled as sweet as chocolate. He doubted he was imagining it.

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert laughed softly. At last, he could laugh aloud, and his five senses slowly grew clear.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert laughed softly. Now that he could make a sound again, his five senses gradually sharpened.

hunks.baseline: The sound of his heartbeat seemed to thunder in his ears.
hunks.sol: His quickening heartbeat thundered in his ears.

hunks.baseline: As his heart pounded faster, the blood pooled in the crater rushed toward its owner’s body.
hunks.sol: As his heart beat faster, the blood pooled in the crater surged toward its owner.

hunks.baseline: But it wasn’t red anymore.
hunks.sol: But it was no longer red.

hunks.baseline: It was a thick, gleaming green—the blood of something no one could call human.
hunks.sol: Thick, gleaming green blood that no one could mistake for a human’s.

hunks.baseline: The same blood as that of the unprecedented monster he’d encountered in Paris, more than thirty years ago, when the city had overflowed with blood and corpses, now filled Michael Silbert from head to toe.
hunks.sol: The same blood spilled by the unprecedented monster he’d encountered in Paris more than thirty years ago, when the city had overflowed with blood and corpses, filled Michael Silbert’s entire body.

hunks.baseline: Along with its endless magical power and Regeneration.
hunks.sol: Its endless magical power and Regeneration came with it.

hunks.baseline: The blood was sucked deep into his body. Severed muscles rejoined. Broken bones and ruined organs mended.
hunks.sol: Blood rushed deep into him. Severed muscles rejoined. Broken bones and ruined organs mended.

hunks.baseline: A short scream rang out, as if to celebrate his return to life from the brink of death.
hunks.sol: A short scream rang out, as though to celebrate his return from the brink of death.

hunks.baseline: It was a victory cry announcing the resurrection of one life—and a death rattle announcing the end of another.
hunks.sol: A celebratory salute for one life restored, and the death cry of another.

hunks.baseline: A middle-aged woman staggered backward, her chest pierced through.
hunks.sol: A middle-aged woman staggered backward with a hole through her chest.

hunks.baseline: Like the filth in the pit Michael Silbert had chosen, she’d built up a splendid record of achievements as a hero of the Great Cataclysm. Even on the brink of death, she drove a dagger into a gap in his damaged armor. Her back arched like a bow.
hunks.sol: A hero of the Great Cataclysm with an impressive record—and filth from the pit Michael Silbert had chosen—even at the brink of death, she drove a dagger into a gap in Jin Taekyung’s damaged armor. Her back arched like a bow.

hunks.baseline: Blood spurted as the spearhead came free.
hunks.sol: The spearhead came free, and blood spurted.

hunks.baseline: In front of the corpse that had crumpled like a rotten log stood a young man, tall as an iron tower. Michael Silbert saw him.
hunks.sol: Before the corpse that crumpled like a rotten log stood a young man, tall as an iron tower.

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert looked at Jin Taekyung. Or rather, Jin Taekyung looked at Michael Silbert.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert looked at Jin Taekyung. No—Jin Taekyung looked at Michael Silbert.

hunks.baseline: At him, with black eyes swallowed by absolute darkness—not the gray of before, not even the whites of his eyes remaining.
hunks.sol: At his eyes, swallowed by utter darkness, with none of their former gray or even their whites remaining.

hunks.baseline: The National Assembly, spanning hundreds of meters across, fell silent for a moment, along with the fierce battlefield that had been nearing its end.
hunks.sol: The National Assembly, spanning hundreds of meters, fell silent. So did the fierce battle within it, just as it had been nearing its end.

hunks.baseline: Everyone was horrified. Everyone fell silent.
At the sight of Michael Silbert, who had completely lost the form of a human being.
hunks.sol: Everyone stared in horror at Michael Silbert, who had lost all semblance of human form.

hunks.baseline: At the scales covering his body, the two horns that had pierced through his forehead, and the name of a monster that flashed into their minds at the sight of the enormous wings resembling darkness.
hunks.sol: Scales covered his body. Two horns jutted from his forehead. At the sight of his vast, dark wings, the name of a monster flashed through their minds.

hunks.baseline: A voice that sounded like a groan slipped between someone’s lips.
hunks.sol: Someone voiced it in a near-groan.

hunks.baseline: The root and very embodiment of the dragonkin, a race born with nightmare-like power.
hunks.sol: The origin and very embodiment of the dragonkin, born with nightmarish power.

hunks.baseline: A monster of the highest order—the oldest and most evil—with magical power that never ran dry, strength that could tear apart heaven and earth, and tremendous Regeneration.
hunks.sol: The oldest and worst of monsters, with magical power that never ran dry, strength enough to tear heaven and earth apart, and tremendous Regeneration.

hunks.baseline: And people suddenly remembered something they’d forgotten.
hunks.sol: Then people remembered a fact they’d forgotten.

hunks.baseline: During the great battle in Paris more than thirty years ago, the battle that made Michael Silbert who he was, it had been a young dragon—not even fully grown yet—that swallowed up a thousand lives, including those of four S-rank Hunters.
hunks.sol: In the great battle in Paris more than thirty years ago—the battle that had made Michael Silbert who he was—the creature that had claimed a thousand lives, including four S-rank Hunters, had been a young Dragon. It hadn’t even reached full maturity.

hunks.baseline: And the Dragon Heart that creature must have possessed had never been found anywhere.
hunks.sol: And its Dragon Heart had never been found.

hunks.baseline: —Yes. Do you understand now?
hunks.sol: —Yes. Now do you understand?

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert laughed loudly.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert laughed aloud.

hunks.baseline: His roar shook the entire National Assembly, and the faces of several people seized by Fear turned deathly pale.
hunks.sol: The roar shook the entire National Assembly, and several people seized by Fear turned deathly pale.

hunks.baseline: But not one man’s.
hunks.sol: But one man did not.

hunks.baseline: Jin Taekyung watched the dreadful mass of energy gathering around the two horns that had sprouted from Michael Silbert’s forehead. Even as he watched the Breath, he wasn’t flustered.
hunks.sol: A dreadful mass of energy gathered around the two horns rising from Michael Silbert’s forehead. Jin Taekyung watched the Breath form without a trace of panic.

hunks.baseline: He merely looked on for a moment before tossing out a single word like a sigh.
hunks.sol: He gazed at it for a moment, then spoke as if sighing.

hunks.baseline: “Fuck, you bastard. I’m already feeling like shit as it is……”
hunks.sol: “Fucking bastard. I’m already in bad shape……”

hunks.baseline: And then, the next moment—
hunks.sol: And the next moment—

hunks.baseline: An immense darkness poured down, staining the whole world, and collided with the blue-white flames swirling along the spearhead.
hunks.sol: Immense darkness poured down, staining the whole world, and collided with blue-white flames swirling along the spearhead.

hunks.baseline: At the end of it all, there was a blinding flash.
hunks.sol: At the end of it all came a blinding flash.
